segments.text: Alright, so summer is here and in my opinion that's really the best time to go out, start filming,
start vlogging and documenting your life. Maybe you've just sat down and scripted out your first
video or maybe you've even gone out and filmed it but I bet in the back of your mind something still
just doesn't feel right about your vlog and I'm gonna say it right now you're probably just
overthinking it. I was too in the very beginning and honestly I still do even to this day but the
entire creative process for vlogging has definitely gotten a lot easier over the years so today I
wanted to share some advice about that. Things I've learned through years of trial and error on how
you can go about your day and start vlogging your life without completely overcomplicating
the process as a beginner.
So essentially a vlog is just a very loosely defined short film.
And what that means is at the core of it all you still need a good story.
I know you are definitely tired of hearing that from everybody that story is king.
You have to have a story because everybody knows that and I know you do too.
See the problem isn't that you don't know that.
It's that you don't know how to actually find a story in your day to tell.
So to break down how I find a story in my day to make a vlog about, I like to think about the fundamental pieces in a movie.
And just like short films, feature films, documentaries, what you really need to think about are scenes.
Just like scenes in your favorite movie, you need to have a compilation of scenes that when stitched together tell a greater and broader story.
When it comes to vlogging, because you're filming as the day is going on, you sometimes don't know that overarching story,
but I bet you do know at least a scene or two ahead.
What that means is maybe I don't know exactly what I'm up to today, but I do know that in an hour or so,
I'm gonna go meet up with a friend so I can build a scene around that and then after that again
I might not know what I'm gonna do for the rest of the evening
But I do know that I'm hungry so I'm gonna go get some food. That's another scene
So instead of stressing yourself before you start shooting of what is my story
Just allow yourself to live life and think of things scene by scene and also think about how the scenes kind of tie into the overall
feeling that you're trying to deliver so when I'm out shooting and filming things
I always try and think is this just a shot that I'm getting because it looks cool
or is this an actual scene if it's a scene
I'll have to build a little bit more around it. Most often I'll also capture some dialogue, some talking,
I'll talk straight to the camera and explain what's going on. A lot of people will tell you that in filmmaking you want to show not tell.
